questions.question: X and Y together can do a piece of work in 30 days. Z alone can do it in 60 days. If they worked together, then in how many days they can finish the work?
questions.solution:
Given:

X and Y can do a work in 30 days, Z can do it alone in 60 days.

Formula:

(1/(X+Y)) + (1/Z) = 1/Total

Calculation:

⇒ (1/30) + (1/60) = 1/Total

⇒ Total = 20 days.

Hence, they can finish the work in 20 days.

questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 44 km/hr and the speed of a stream is 26 km/hr. Find the upstream speed of boat.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

The **upstream speed** is simply the **relative speed** when the boat moves against the current.

Upstream Speed = **Still water speed** − **Stream speed**

Upstream Speed = 44 − 26 = 18 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Speed of boat in still water (u) = 44 km/hr

Speed of the stream (v) = 26 km/hr

**Formula Used:**

Upstream speed = u − v

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/174563aee39294acc2fe063e3a47ba5a4cb6eaae64cf336963613a2abc084b7f.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Upstream speed = Speed of boat in still water − Speed of stream

⇒ Upstream speed = 44 − 26

⇒ Upstream speed = 18 km/hr

**∴ The correct answer is 18 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Downstream Speed

It is the speed of the boat when it travels with the flow of the stream. Downstream Speed = u + v.

Still Water Speed Calculation

If downstream (D) and upstream (U) speeds are known, Boat speed (u) = 1/2 × (D + U).

Stream Speed Calculation

If downstream (D) and upstream (U) speeds are known, Stream speed (v) = 1/2 × (D − U).</p

questions.question: The price of sugar is increased by 40%. By what percentage must one cut down on the consumption of sugar so that no extra amount has to be incurred on sugar?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Using the fractional reduction rule for constant expenditure:

Price increase = 40% = 2/5

If price increases by a fraction a/b, consumption must decrease by a/(a+b) to keep expenditure constant.

Required consumption reduction = 2 / (2 + 5) = 2/7

Percentage reduction = (2 ÷ 7) × 100 = 28.57% ≈ 28.5%

**∴ The correct answer is 28.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Percentage increase in the price of sugar = 40%

**Concept Used:**

When Expenditure remains constant, Price and Consumption are inversely proportional (Expenditure = Price × Consumption).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9e1e2dc75ad8d79ab530897b421bac313d7e946174f1eec10b033b01453d8b55.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the initial price of sugar be ₹100 per unit and initial consumption be 100 units.

⇒ Initial Expenditure = 100 × 100 = ₹10000

⇒ New price of sugar after 40% increase = ₹140 per unit

⇒ To keep the expenditure constant at ₹10000, New Consumption = 10000 ÷ 140 = 500 / 7 units

⇒ Reduction in consumption = Original Consumption − New Consumption

⇒ Reduction in consumption = 100 − (500 / 7) = (700 − 500) / 7 = 200 / 7 units

⇒ Percentage reduction = [(Reduction in consumption) ÷ (Original Consumption)] × 100

⇒ Percentage reduction = [(200 / 7) ÷ 100] × 100

⇒ Percentage reduction = 200 / 7 % = 28.57%

⇒ Looking at the options, it is approximately 28.5%.

**∴ The correct answer is 28.5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Price & Consumption Rule (Increase)

If the price of a commodity increases by R%, the required percentage reduction in consumption so as not to increase the overall expenditure is given by [R ÷ (100 + R)] × 100%.

Price & Consumption Rule (Decrease)

If the price of a commodity decreases by R%, the permissible percentage increase in consumption to maintain the exact same expenditure is given by [R ÷ (100 − R)] × 100%.

Constant Product Rule

For any equation of the form A × B = Constant, if variable A increases by a fraction of x/y, then variable B must decrease by the fraction x/(x+y) to keep their product constant.

questions.question: P alone can complete a work in 15 days and Q alone can complete the same work in 12 days. They start the work together but after 3 days P leaves the work. How much time will Q take to finish the remaining work?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total work = LCM(15, 12) = 60 units.

Efficiency of P = 60 ÷ 15 = 4 units/day | Efficiency of Q = 60 ÷ 12 = 5 units/day.

Work done together in 3 days = 3 × (4 + 5) = 27 units.

Remaining time for Q = (60 − 27) ÷ 5 = 33 ÷ 5 = 6.6 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.6 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by P to complete the work = 15 days.

Time taken by Q to complete the work = 12 days.

P and Q work together for 3 days, then P leaves.

**Method Used:**

LCM Method: Total Work = LCM of individual days.

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time taken.

 
 

 **Person**
 **Days**
 **Total Work**
 **Efficiency**

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total work = 60 units.

⇒ Combined efficiency of P and Q = 4 + 5 = 9 units/day.

⇒ Work completed by P and Q in 3 days = 9 × 3 = 27 units.

⇒ Remaining work = 60 − 27 = 33 units.

⇒ Time taken by Q to finish the remaining work = Remaining work ÷ Q's efficiency.

⇒ Time taken by Q = 33 ÷ 5 = 6.6 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 6.6 days.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Fractional Work Method

If a person completes a job in x days, then the part of the work completed in 1 day is 1/x. Work remaining after n days is 1 − (n ÷ x).

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the actual work done by the individuals. If they work for the same number of days, wages are distributed in the ratio of their efficiencies.

Pipes and Cisterns

The concept of time and work directly applies to pipes and cisterns. Filling a tank is considered positive work, while emptying a tank is considered negative work.

questions.question: Three metal rods of length 77 cm, 110 cm and 121 cm are to be cut into parts of equal length. Each part must be as long as possible. What is the maximum number of pieces that can be cut?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

To get pieces as long as possible, length of each piece must be HCF(77, 110, 121).

HCF(77, 110, 121) = 11 cm.

Total pieces = (Length 1 ÷ HCF) + (Length 2 ÷ HCF) + (Length 3 ÷ HCF)

Total pieces = (77 ÷ 11) + (110 ÷ 11) + (121 ÷ 11)

Total pieces = 7 + 10 + 11 = 28.

**∴ The correct option is B.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Lengths of metal rods = 77 cm, 110 cm, 121 cm.

**Formula Used:**

Maximum length of each part = HCF of rod lengths.

Total number of pieces = (Total length of all rods) ÷ (Length of one part).

 110 cm (10 × 11 cm)

 121 cm (11 × 11 cm)

 Each segment length = HCF(77, 110, 121) = 11 cm

**Calculations:**

⇒ Prime factors of 77 = 7 × 11

⇒ Prime factors of 110 = 2 × 5 × 11

⇒ Prime factors of 121 = 11 × 11

⇒ HCF (77, 110, 121) = 11 cm

⇒ Max length of each part = 11 cm

⇒ Number of pieces from Rod 1 = 77 ÷ 11 = 7

⇒ Number of pieces from Rod 2 = 110 ÷ 11 = 10

⇒ Number of pieces from Rod 3 = 121 ÷ 11 = 11

⇒ Total maximum pieces = 7 + 10 + 11 = 28

**∴ The correct option is B.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF (Highest Common Factor)

It is the greatest number that divides each of the given numbers exactly without leaving any remainder.

Cutting Problems

When objects of different lengths are cut into equal pieces of maximum possible length, that length is always the HCF of the original lengths.

Number of Pieces Formula

Total Pieces = (Σ Lengths) ÷ HCF. Here, (77 + 110 + 121) ÷ 11 = 308 ÷ 11 = 28.</p

• Chemical energy__ is converted into electrical energy by a battery.

 __
 
• A battery is a device that stores chemical energy and converts it to electrical energy.
 
• The chemical reactions in a battery involve the flow of electrons from one material (electrode) to another, through an external circuit.
 
• The flow of electrons provides an electric current that can be used to do work.
 
• To balance the flow of electrons, charged ions also flow through an electrolyte solution that is in contact with both electrodes.
 
• A battery can be made up of one or several electrochemical cells.
 
• The invention of the battery as we know it is credited to the Italian scientist Alessandro Volta.​

 Explanation
 Example
 
 
 
 

 Chemical Energy into Light Energy
 This transformation occurs when energy stored in chemical bonds is released as light energy.
 A glow stick is an example of this. The chemical reaction inside the glow stick releases energy in the form of light.
 
 

 Mechanical Energy into Chemical Energy
 This transformation occurs when mechanical energy, or work, is used to produce chemical energy.
 In photosynthesis, plants use the mechanical energy of photon particles (light) to transform carbon dioxide and water into glucose (chemical energy).
 
 

 Chemical Energy into Sound Energy
